bull.b: Term-based subscriptions provide recurring revenue visibility, while expanding users, geographies, modules and product coverage can deepen customer relationships. This combination supports durable retention economics and gives Zscaler multiple paths to grow account value over the next several quarters.

Strong top-line and ARR growth, together with rising large-customer penetration, indicates broad enterprise demand rather than reliance on isolated contracts. Larger deployments can increase platform integration and create a durable base for additional products, users and workloads.

High gross margins and substantial positive cash flow demonstrate attractive SaaS economics despite ongoing GAAP losses. Strong cash conversion provides resources for product development, infrastructure investment and strategic initiatives while supporting financial flexibility over the medium term.

bear.b: Continued negative EBIT and net income show that accounting profitability has not yet been established. Although improving EBITDA and non-GAAP margins are encouraging, the absence of sustained GAAP earnings can constrain the durability of reported profitability and leaves execution dependent on continued growth.

Management expects a meaningful deceleration from fiscal 2026 growth to mid-teen expansion in fiscal 2027. Slower growth can reduce operating leverage, make customer expansion more important and increase pressure on execution as Zscaler scales from a larger revenue base.

bear.t: Higher investment and integration execution risk
bear.b: Higher infrastructure spending can weigh on free cash flow margins, while Red Canary’s elevated MDR churn and workforce restructuring create execution demands. These pressures may divert management attention and delay the contribution of newer offerings during the next several quarters.
